title: Signal Probeboard: weekly bench sync notes
content:
Attendees: Aisha (note), Marcus, Sofia, Evan, Priya, on-call SRE (Ken).

Purpose: weekly perf + benchmark sync focused on recent tail-latency regression observed after the kernel-selection rollout (10/10). We captured new probe runs across three machine shapes, two sequence distributions, and both prefix-KV enabled/disabled. This doc summarizes observed signals, quick hypotheses, run artifacts, and assigned actions.

High-level summary:
- Signal: p99 tail latency increased on long-sequence (>256 tokens) synthetic chat workload after kernel rollout. Impact visible on both hosted and dedicated pools but worse on T4-like shapes.
- Scope: regression reproducible in lab with replayed production traces; not present in the pre-rollout snapshot.
- Severity: P1 for SLA-sensitive routes (canary traffic flagged); mitigated via temporary routing to fallback model-quantized variants.

What we ran (short):
- Baseline (pre-rollout snapshot): model: rwd-v1-7b-fp16, batch=8, seq_dist: mixed(64/128/512), KV cache ON, shape: gtx-t4/rtx-a10. Result summary: p50=7.8ms, p90=21ms, p99=62ms (seq512 p99 ~= 110ms).
- Post-rollout (kernel v2.3.1): same parameters. Result summary: p50=8.9ms, p90=26ms, p99=145ms (seq512 p99 spiked to ~320ms occasionally).
- Isolated long-seq test (only seq512): p99 jump from 110ms -> 310ms.
- KV disabled: reduced p99 but increased p50 slightly; suggests interaction between new kernels and KV cache path.
- Small-batch stress (batch=1..4): tail variance increased under low-concurrency load, which is consistent with our observed production microbursts.

Notable raw observations:
- Spike frequency: intermittent(10-12% of requests in long-seq windows) producing outliers; spikes correlate with particular attention-kernel selection (kernel id K-AO-14 in trace metadata).
- Memory temp: small bump in GPU DRAM alloc/free cycles during spike windows.
- CPU driver logs show a short (1-5ms) stall prior to heavy attention compute for the spiking requests.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel-selection heuristic in v2.3.1 sometimes picks a slower attention kernel for particular token shapes leading to serialization amplifying p99.
2) KV cache layout change + new kernel increases register pressure causing occasional fallback to a slower code path.
3) Host-side scheduling (CUDA streams interaction) resulting in micro-contention that propagates into tail latency; more visible when batch sizes are small and seq lengths large.
4) Data-dependent quantization path not exercised in baseline; fallback path costs more on some tokens.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Canary routing: redirected 100% of canary traffic to fallback runtime variant (kernel v2.2.7) for 24h.
- Model variant: pinned heavy customers to quantized-compat variant (rwd-v1-7b-q4) for affected API routes.
- Alerting: added temporary alert for 95th->99th lat jump > 2x baseline for seq>256.

Detailed experiment plan (next 48h):
A) Kernel microbench matrix (owners: Marcus + Evan)
  - Reproduce locally with microbench harness that forces kernel id selection.
  - Steps: run 100k inferences for seq=64/256/512, batch=1/4/8, KV on/off across shapes a10/t4.
  - Metrics: p50/p90/p99, histogram of kernel ids, GPU utilization, per-request host-stall metric.
  - Target: identify exact kernel id(s) tied to outliers.

B) KV layout rollback test (owner: Sofia)
  - Deploy variant that uses previous KV memory layout with new kernels enabled.
  - Rationale: check interaction surface.
  - Run against production replay (s3://bench-logs/2026-10-14/replay-longseq.json).

C) Stream scheduling probe (owner: Priya + SRE Ken)
  - Insert extra tracing around CUDA stream submits and host synchronization points in the runtime for failing flows.
  - Goal: confirm or rule out host-side stalls.

D) Acceptance criteria for rollback/unblock:
  - p99(seq512) returns to within 1.2x of baseline (pre-rollout snapshot) for three consecutive 30-minute runs under production-replay.
  - No new error traces or OOMs introduced.

Notes from quick debug session (10/14 afternoon):
- Marcus attached a flamegraph showing two distinct slow paths inside attention: one median-heavy (expected) and one with extra memcpy and a fallback loop.
- Evan confirmed kernel selector has heuristic threshold tuned by sequence length and a recent commit relaxed the threshold, which can prefer AO-kernel for some token-per-iteration patterns.
- Sofia reproduced the p99 on RTX-A10 but at lower spike amplitude than T4; implies architecture-specific kernel perf.

Open questions / things to verify:
- Which token patterns trigger the selector change? Need to link with tokenizer/bytepair boundaries. (action: Marcus to sample 1k spiking inputs and dump tokenization).
- Is there a measurable difference across driver versions? (action: SRE to run a short driver-rollback test on a staging node).
- Can we add a fast-path check in selector to prefer previously-known-good kernels for long sequences until we have a permanent fix? (action: Evan explore a cheap guard with minimal perf cost).

Planned timeline and communication:
- 10/14 evening: pivot to fallback runtime for canary (done).
- 10/15 morning: kernel microbench results expected (Marcus/Evan).
- 10/15 afternoon: KV layout rollback run (Sofia).
- 10/16: decision on whether to ship a hotfix that reverts selector heuristic or to roll back kernel release entirely.
- Customer comms: CS draft ready if rollback is required; notify top-20 customers by 10/16 EOD if route changes persist. (owner CS: Lila Gomez)

Action items (owner - due):
- Marcus: run kernel-id sampling harness and upload kernel-id->request sample map to s3 (due: 2026-10-15 10:00).
- Evan: prototype cheap selector guard and benchmark overhead (due: 2026-10-15 18:00).
- Sofia: KV-rollback replay run and summary (due: 2026-10-15 18:00).
- Priya/Ken: instrument host-side stream traces on 2 staging nodes and share traces (due: 2026-10-15 noon).
- Aisha: update canary routing policy and monitor alerts (ongoing).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the microbench harness deterministic seeds; we've seen stochastic noise when RNGs differ across nodes.
- Remember to annotate test logs with driver/kernel/compiler versions.
- Save full flamegraphs under s3://bench-logs/2026-10-14/signal-probeboard/flamegraphs/ for postmortem.

Appendix - quick commands used during session:
- run replay: ./tools/replay-run --trace s3://bench-logs/2026-10-14/replay-longseq.json --model rwd-v1-7b-fp16 --batch 8 --kv true --out s3://bench-logs/2026-10-14/signal-probeboard/run1.json
- microbench: ./tools/microbench --kernel-force "auto" --seq 512 --iters 100000 --shape t4 --out local/micro-t4-512.json
- kernel-id dump: ./runtime/bin/dump-kernel-ids --trace-id <id> --out /tmp/ids.json

If new folks join: start with the TL;DR at top and then jump to experiment plan A->D.

Next sync: daily short standup (15m) 10/15 09:30 to triage results. Full writeup and retrospective after root cause confirmed.

-- Aisha
